extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to BMC Medicine (biomedical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, licensing, and submitting manuscripts (and supporting files) to the open‑access journal BMC Medicine, including peer review and transfer policies. Covers required file types, data and figure standards, cover letter contents, and APC/licensing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal. BMC Medicine publishes outstanding and influential research in all areas of clinical practice, translational medicine, medical and health advances, public health, global health, policy, and general topics of interest to the biomedical and sociomedical professional communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should verify their manuscript fits the journal’s scope before submission so it reaches the right audience; consult the Aims and scope page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC) and payment terms
rubrics_metrics.description: An article processing charge (APC) applies for each article accepted for publication in BMC Medicine. The current APC for BMC Medicine is £3190.00 GBP / $4490.00 USD / €3690.00 EUR. This fee is subject to VAT or local taxes where applicable. The APC price is determined from the date on which the article is accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APC subject to country‑tiered pricing pilot; check applicable APC for your country. APC waivers/discounts policies and open access support portals provide further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access licensing options
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC Medicine articles are published open access under a CC BY-NC-ND (Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives 4.0) or CC BY (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0) licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CC BY-NC-ND: share for non-commercial purposes with attribution; permission required for commercial re-use or adapted derivatives. CC BY: may be shared and adapted for any purpose (including commercially) with attribution. Authors may need other licence variations to meet funder/institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: APC waivers and discounts policy and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers APC waivers and discounts for corresponding authors based in the world’s lowest income countries; requests for discretionary APC waivers and discounts from other authors will be considered case-by-case and may be granted in cases of financial need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications for discretionary APC waivers and discounts should be made at the point of manuscript submission; requests made during review or after acceptance cannot be considered. The country‑tiered APC pilot supersedes some previous waivers/discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript must be submitted by an author
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a co-author initiates submission; do not use third‑party submission services to submit on behalf of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting: spacing, numbering, units, characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; ensure special characters are embedded in text; do not use page breaks in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding special characters prevents loss during PDF conversion. Avoid manual page breaks which may disrupt processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable main manuscript file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable editable file formats for the main manuscript document: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich text format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editable files are required for production processing. If non-editable files (e.g., PDFs) are submitted, authors will be required to re-submit editable versions when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX/TeX source requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template. A PDF of your manuscript files will be compiled during submission using pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021. All relevant editable source files must be uploaded during submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit source files will cause delays in production. Follow the Springer Nature template to reduce conversion issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: All BioMed Central journals strongly encourage or require authors to provide all datasets on which the conclusions rely. Datasets may be deposited in publicly available repositories or presented in the main paper or additional supporting files. Provide datasets in machine-readable formats (e.g., spreadsheets rather than PDFs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where community expectations exist for data archiving in public repositories, submission to a community-endorsed public repository is mandatory. Do not link to data on personal/departmental websites; include data as additional files or in repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting the 'Availability of data and materials' section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an 'Availability of data and materials' section using the required formats: e.g., "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink to dataset(s) in https:// format]." Or, if included as additional files: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) included within the article (and its additional file(s))."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact phrasing templates provided in the guidelines to ensure clarity and consistency for readers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation and referencing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: BioMed Central endorses the Force11 Data Citation Principles and requires that all publicly available datasets be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or unique identifier such as a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For databases, state the web/ftp address and any use restrictions in the 'Availability' section. Cite data with persistent identifiers in the reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For software, include: Project name; Project home page; Archived version DOI or unique identifier (e.g., Zenodo); Operating system(s); Programming language; Other requirements; License; Any restrictions to use by non-academics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient metadata so others can access and run the software; include archived releases with DOIs where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion: what may be cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers, may be cited. Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list, but may be included in the text as 'unpublished observations' or 'personal communications' with names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission before quoting personal communications. Only footnotes are permitted; follow Index Medicus/MEDLINE journal abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting and web links
rubrics_metrics.description: Web links and URLs, including links to authors' own websites, should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text. Provide full details: title, URL, and date accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided. Authors may use reference management software to ensure correct formatting. In-press articles needed for reviewer assessment should be made available if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be numbered in the order they are first mentioned in the text, and uploaded in this order. Multi-panel figures should be submitted as a single composite file that contains all parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload individual figure files in the order cited in the manuscript to aid processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure titles and legends placement and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure titles (max 15 words) and legends (max 300 words) should be provided in the main manuscript, not in the graphic file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep titles concise (<=15 words) and legends informative but within the 300-word limit; do not place legend text inside figure image files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure keys and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic, not into the legend of the figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed keys directly in the image to avoid misplacement during layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure cropping, legibility and line/font requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should be closely cropped to minimise white space. Figures should be designed so all information, including text, is legible at final dimensions. All lines should be wider than 0.25 pt when constrained to standard figure widths. All fonts must be embedded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design figures for legibility at 600/1200 pixel web widths and PDF widths (85 mm or 170 mm). Ensure fonts are embedded to avoid substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure image resolution and sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Image resolution approximately 300 dpi at final size. Figures on the web: width of 600 pixels (standard), 1200 pixels (high resolution). Figures in the final PDF: width of 85 mm (half page) or 170 mm (full page), maximum height of 225 mm for figure and legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure resolution and dimensions so text and symbols remain legible at publication sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure file types and file size limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted figure file formats: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX. Individual figure files should not exceed 10 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate formats for type of content (vector vs photographic). Keep individual files under 10 MB for upload convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file compression and conversion guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector figures should be submitted as PDF where possible. TIFF files should be saved with LZW compression (lossless). JPEG files should be saved at maximum quality. Minimise conversion between file types (especially lossy formats such as JPEG) to avoid degradation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these recommendations to preserve quality and reduce upload times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for reproduced figures and indication
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the author(s) to obtain permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables previously published elsewhere. Permission should be indicated in the figure legend, and the original source included in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For open access publication, ensure permissions cover OA distribution; include permission statements in legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering, citation and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be numbered and cited in the text in sequence using Arabic numerals. Tables less than one A4/Letter page can be placed in the appropriate location within the manuscript. Tables larger than one A4/Letter page can be placed at the end of the document; indicate where they should appear in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For very wide or large tables, upload as additional files and cite their intended location in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table file formats, titles, legends and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabular data provided as additional files can be uploaded as Excel (.xls) or CSV (.csv). Table titles (max 15 words) should be included above the table, and legends (max 300 words) underneath. Tables should be formatted using the 'Table object' function in your word processor; do not embed as figures or spreadsheet images. Color and shading may not be used. Commas should not be used to indicate numerical values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use superscript, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold text to highlight parts of a table and explain them in the legend. Ensure numeric formatting follows the no‑comma rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: allowed content and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can provide datasets, tables, movies, or other information as additional files. All additional files will be published along with the accepted article. Do not include files such as patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised versions of the main manuscript document with tracked changes. Do not include any individual participant details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested, files such as consent forms should be sent by email to the editorial office quoting the manuscript reference number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: maximum size, naming and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum file size for additional files is 20 MB each; files will be virus-scanned on submission. Each additional file should be cited in sequence within the main body of text and named 'Additional file 1' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference additional files explicitly by file name within the text (e.g., 'see Additional file 1'). Avoid linking to external personal websites for supplementary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: required metadata and format information
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing additional material, list the following in a separate section of the manuscript text: File name; File format including correct extension; Title of data; Description of data. For unusual formats include a URL of an appropriate viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear metadata to help readers and editors access and interpret supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality expectation and optional services
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting your work in well-written English gives the best chance for editors and reviewers to understand it. Using language editing services is not a requirement for publication and does not imply or guarantee acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include English language tutorials, colleague review, or professional language editing services (Springer Nature Author Services) and an AI-based language quality checker (AJE). Discounts may be available for first-time users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter should include: an explanation of why your manuscript should be published in BMC Medicine; an explanation of any issues relating to journal policies; a declaration of any potential competing interests; confirmation that all authors have approved the manuscript for submission; confirmation that the content has not been published or submitted elsewhere. If submitting to a special issue, state its name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any additional information requested in instructions for your specific article type. Use the cover letter to flag potential policy issues or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding peer reviewers (author suggestions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In your cover letter, you may suggest potential peer reviewers for your manuscript. Provide institutional email addresses where possible, or identifiers (ORCID/Scopus ID) to help verify identity. You may also enter details of anyone you prefer not to review your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally falsifying reviewer information (false names/emails) will result in rejection and possible further investigation under the misconduct policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically two or more experts evaluate each manuscript based on three main criteria: scientific robustness (is the methodology sound and data support conclusions?), originality (does the research duplicate existing work?), and clarity (is the manuscript clear and coherent enough for publication?). Editors make decisions based on reviewers' reports and may consult the editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods are rigorous, novelty is clear, and writing is sufficiently clear for reviewers to assess; include any in-press references if necessary for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC Medicine operates a transparent peer review system where, if the article is published, the reviewer reports are published online alongside the article under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 but the reviewer is not named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review reports may be published and serve educational purposes; reviewers and editors must declare competing interests and can be excluded if a conflict exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests by reviewers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests and can be excluded from the peer review process if a competing interest exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any potential conflicts when participating in review or editorial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer process and author control
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript transfer allows resubmission of your manuscript and any reviewer comments to another journal within the publisher’s portfolio. Transfer is voluntary: your manuscript will not be transferred without your input. If you decline the transfer, your file will be closed. You may withdraw a transfer at any point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits of transfer: choice of alternative journals, no reformatting necessary, save time. The Transfer Desk assists authors with matching journals and personal assistance; authors must agree to transfers and complete submission to the new journal.
